messages.text:
My wife, Duygu Ceylan, has an oldschool website, where updating requires a lot of manual work: https://duygu-ceylan.com

My website is more programmatical. In other terms, I have a bibliography file (`*.bib`) and a resume as a JSON file, and the website renders everything about me using these two files. On top of that I add news and other links using markdown and a YML file: https://kaanaksit.com

Firstly, initiate a git repository in the current folder, and leave the remote blank for now. I want you to help me to make a website for my wife, where she could programmatically update her public facing information with ease.

# [Duygu Ceylan](https://www.duygu-ceylan.com/)

## Research Scientist

- [Home](https://www.duygu-ceylan.com/)

![Duygu Ceylan]( "Duygu Ceylan")

[![SONY DSC](http://www.duygu-ceylan.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/profile2-225x300.jpg)](http://www.duygu-ceylan.com/contact/sony-dsc/)

Principal Research Scientist

Adobe Research London

e-mail: duygu.ceylan@gmail.com

I am a principal research scientist at [Adobe Research](http://www.adobe.com/technology.html "http://www.adobe.com/technology.html"). Prior to joining Adobe in 2014, I obtained my PhD degree from [EPFL](http://www.epfl.ch/ "http://www.epfl.ch/") where I worked with [Prof. Mark Pauly](http://lgg.epfl.ch/people.php?p=1 "http://lgg.epfl.ch/people.php?p=1"). I graduated from Computer Engineering Department of [METU](http://metu.edu.tr/ "http://metu.edu.tr/") in 2007 and got my Master’s degree in CS from [Bilkent University](http://www.bilkent.edu.tr/index.html "http://www.bilkent.edu.tr/index.html") in 2009\. During my Master’s studies I also worked as a software engineer at [Aselsan Inc.](http://www.aselsan.com.tr/default.asp?lang=en "http://www.aselsan.com.tr/default.asp?lang=en")

I received the Eurographics PhD Award in 2015 and the Eurographics Young Researcher Award in 2020\.

My research interests include using machine learning techniques to infer and analyze 3D information from images and videos, and utilize this to generate and edit 2D and 3D content. I'm excited to work at the intersection of computer vision and graphics where I look for new methods to bridge the gap between 2D & 3D.

If you're interested in doing a research internship with me or joining my group at Adobe Research please send me an email with your resume and research interests.

# Kaan Akşit

*Associate Professor of Computational Light at University College London*, [Optica Fellow](https://www.optica.org/about/newsroom/news_releases/2025/optica_announces_2026_fellows_class/), [IEEE Senior Member](https://ieee-collabratec.ieee.org/app/p/KaanAksit1110065), [SPIE Senior Member](https://spie.org/profile/kaanaksit), [Optica Intelligent Interfaces and Displays Technology Chair](https://www.optica.org//en-us/get_involved/technical_groups/iapd/display_technology_\(it\)/), [ACM TOG Associate Editor](https://dl.acm.org/journal/tog/editorial-board), [ACM and ACM SIGGRAPH Member](https://dl.acm.org/profile/99658680272)

![kaan_aksit.png](/assets/img/kaan_aksit.png?dc7213adedae8f1578252454f5480f71)

kaanaksit@kaanaksit.com

[*Kaan Akşit*](https://kaanaksit.com) is an Associate Professor of Computational Light in the [`Computer Science Department`](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/computer-science/) at [`University College London`](https://www.ucl.ac.uk) in the United Kingdom, where he also leads the [`Computational Light Laboratory`](https://complightlab.com). He received his Ph.D. in electrical engineering from [`Koç University`](https://ku.edu.tr), Türkiye[`*`](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/jun/03/turkey-changes-name-to-turkiye-as-other-name-is-for-the-birds), in 2014\. He received his M.Sc. degree in electrical power engineering from [`RWTH Aachen University`](https://www.rwth-aachen.de), Germany, in 2010\. He received his B.S. in electrical engineering from [`Istanbul Technical University`](https://www.itu.edu.tr), Türkiye, in 2007\. His research focuses on the intersection of light and computation, including artificial intelligence assisted computational approaches in imaging, graphics, fabrication, and displays. His work is widely known among the optics and graphics community for his contributions to display technologies dedicated to 3D, virtual reality, and augmented reality. He worked as a research intern at [`Philips Research`](https://www.philips.com/a-w/about/innovation/research.html), the Netherlands, and [`Disney Research`](https://studios.disneyresearch.com/), Switzerland, in 2009 and 2013, respectively. In addition, he was a Senior Research Scientist at [`NVIDIA`](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/research/), the United States of America, from 2014 to 2020\. Over the years, his research has been recognized with numerous awards from various highly respected venues and institutions including [`ACM SIGGRAPH`](https://www.siggraph.org/), [`IEEE VR and ISMAR`](https://ieeevr.org/) and [`Optica`](https://www.optica.org/).

**Prospective Students:** Students interested in completing their master’s thesis in the domains of computational displays, computational imaging, perceptual graphics, physically informed deep learning models, generative models in physical sciences, and optical computing, they can reach out via email for more details. Students are encouraged to reach out via email for [`open Ph.D. studentships`](https://complightlab.com/documentation/become_phd_student/) and research intern positions with their resume and research statements.

**Keywords:** [`Computational Light`](https://kaanaksit.com/odak/course/), [`Computational Displays`](https://kaanaksit.com/assets/pdf/KoulierisEtAl_Eurographics2019_Near_eye_display_and_tracking_technologies_for_virtual_and_augmented_reality.pdf), [`Perceptual Graphics`](https://doi.org/10.1145/2077434.2077448), [`Optical Computing`](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42254-023-00645-5)

**Websites:** [`Personal website`](https://kaanaksit.com), [`Computational Light Laboratory`](https://complightlab.com), [`Odak Toolkit`](https://github.com/kaanaksit/odak)

**Public engagements:** [`High-Beams Seminars`](https://complightlab.com/outreach/), [`Research Hub`](https://complightlab.com/outreach/)

==== AGENTS.md ====
# Tools
- For web search, use the `ddg-search` tool.
- For PDF reading, use the `pdf-reader` tool.
- For emails, I typically use the `thunderbird-mcp` tool.

# Python tools
- When using Python, I use my library, `odak`, wherever I can. The source code of my library is typically found under `~/repos/odak` on my computers.
- For Python image loading, use `odak.learn.tools.load_image` (e.g., `odak.learn.tools.load_image("image.png", normalizeby=255.0, torch_style=True)`).
- For Python image saving, use `odak.learn.tools.save_image` (e.g., `odak.learn.tools.save_image("image.png", image, cmin=0.0, cmax=1.0)`).

# Publications
- When a publication is found online, provide its Digital Object Identifier (DOI) alongside it.
- Always double check that any identified publication truly exists before citing it. No publication hallucination is allowed.

# Writing style
- Never use em dashes. Use commas, periods, or parentheses instead.
- Never use apostrophes/contractions. Prefer full forms (e.g., "I have" instead of "I've"). This also includes possessive apostrophes. Reword to avoid them (e.g., "their institutions" instead of "the authors' institutions").
- Never use semicolons. End the sentence with a full stop and start a new sentence instead. This keeps the text more readable.
- Never use a colon (:) in prose. End the clause with a period or comma and continue as a new sentence or phrase. This does not apply to URLs, times, code, or the commit message format.
- Enumerate with bullet points (dash items), not numbered lists.
- Do not use bold text (avoid ** markers) or other heavy Markdown emphasis in written prose.
- When writing a document using LaTeX, write a new line for every sentence.
- Write in the present tense and active voice.
- Introduce acronyms in Chicago style, capitalizing the full name, as in "Spatial Light Modulator (SLM)" rather than "spatial light modulator (SLM)".

# Commit message rules
- Always use the following format for commit messages: `<emoji> <topic>: <message>`.

==== install.sh ====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPO_URL="${REPO_URL:-git@miystachio.com:git/ceylan}"
DEST_DIR="${DEST_DIR:-$HOME/.config/opencode}"

tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmpdir"' EXIT

git clone --depth 1 "$REPO_URL" "$tmpdir/repo"

mkdir -p "$DEST_DIR"
cp "$tmpdir/repo/AGENTS.md" "$DEST_DIR/AGENTS.md"
cp "$tmpdir/repo/opencode.json" "$DEST_DIR/opencode.json"

echo "Copied AGENTS.md and opencode.json to $DEST_DIR"

==== update.sh ====
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

DEST_DIR="${DEST_DIR:-$HOME/.config/opencode}"
REPO_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
FILES=(AGENTS.md opencode.json)

missing=0
for file in "${FILES[@]}"; do
    if [[ ! -f "$DEST_DIR/$file" ]]; then
        echo "Error: $DEST_DIR/$file not found" >&2
        missing=1
    fi
done
[[ $missing -eq 0 ]]

for file in "${FILES[@]}"; do
    if ! diff -q "$DEST_DIR/$file" "$REPO_DIR/$file" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        cp "$DEST_DIR/$file" "$REPO_DIR/$file"
        echo "Updated $REPO_DIR/$file from $DEST_DIR/$file"
    else
        echo "No changes for $REPO_DIR/$file"
    fi
done

def parse_bib(text):
    entries=[]
    i=0; n=len(text)
    while i<n:
        ch=text[i]
        if ch=='@':
            # read entry type
            j=i+1
            while j<n and (text[j].isalpha() or text[j]=='-'):
                j+=1
            etype=text[i+1:j]
            if etype.lower() in ('comment','preamble','string'):
                # Skip to matching close brace
                i=skip_braced(text,j)
                continue
            # expect '{'
            k=j
            while k<n and text[k] not in '{[':
                k+=1
            # k at position of opening brace
            open_b=text[k]
            close_b='}' if open_b=='{' else ']'
            # Read up to matching close, respecting nested braces
            depth=0; k2=k+1
            while k2<n:
                if text[k2]=='{': depth+=1
                elif text[k2]=='}':
                    depth-=1
                    if depth==0: break
                k2+=1
            body=text[k+1:k2]
            i=k2+1
            # Parse fields: first line up to comma is key
            # Split body into field assignments using top-level commas
            key, fields = split_fields(body)
            entries.append({"key":key,"type":etype,"fields":fields})
        else:
            i+=1
    return entries

split_fields: split top-level commas, but commas inside braces/quotes don't count.

```
def split_fields(body):
    parts=[]; depth=0; cur=[]; inquote=None
    i=0; n=len(body)
    while i<n:
        c=body[i]
        if inquote:
            cur.append(c)
            if c==inquote and body[i-1]!='\\':
                inquote=None
        elif c=='{':
            depth+=1; cur.append(c)
        elif c=='}':
            depth-=1; cur.append(c)
        elif c=='"' or c=="'":
            inquote=c; cur.append(c)
        elif c==',' and depth==0:
            parts.append(''.join(cur).strip()); cur=[]
        else:
            cur.append(c)
        i+=1
    if ''.join(cur).strip():
        parts.append(''.join(cur).strip())
    # first part = key
    key=parts[0].strip()
    fields={}
    for p in parts[1:]:
        if '=' not in p: continue
        name, val = p.split('=',1)
        name=name.strip().lower()
        val=val.strip()
        val = clean_value(val)
        fields[name]=val
    return key, fields
```

clean_value: strip surrounding quotes, or strip braces and collapse whitespace.
```
def clean_value(v):
    v=v.strip()
    if v.startswith('{') and v.endswith('}'):
        v=v[1:-1]
    elif len(v)>=2 and v[0]==v[-1] and v[0] in '"\'':
        v=v[1:-1]
    # Collapse multiple whitespace/newlines
    v=re.sub(r'\s+',' ', v).strip()
    return v
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Build the static website from plain-text source files. Reads: data/resume.json - who the site is about (identity, socials, awards, ...) data/publications.bib - every publication in the "Publications" section news/*.md - one file per news item (YAML front matter + Markdown) templates/site.html - the Jinja2 layout assets/* - static assets (style.css, main.js, profile.jpg, ...) Writes: dist/ - a self-contained static site, ready to host anywhere Usage: python3 build.py """ import calendar import glob import json import os import re import shutil import sys try: import markdown except ImportError: markdown = None try: import yaml except ImportError: yaml = None from jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) # --------------------------------------------------------------- utilities def read(path): with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh: return fh.read() def write(path, text): os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True) with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh: fh.write(text) def month_name(num): num = int(num) return calendar.month_name[num] if 1 <= num <= 12 else "" def fmt_date(raw): s = str(raw).strip()[:10] parts = s.split("-") if len(parts) != 3 or not parts[1].isdigit(): return s y, m, d = parts name = month_name(m) return f"{int(d)} {name} {y}" if name else s def norm_ws(s): return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s or "").strip() # --------------------------------------------------------------- bib parser def _clean_value(v): v = v.strip() if len(v) >= 2 and v[0] in "\"'": v = v[1:-1] elif v.startswith("{") and v.endswith("}"): v = v[1:-1] return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", v).strip() def _split_top(body, sep=","): """Split on top-level separators, ignoring those nested in braces or quotes.""" parts, cur = [], [] depth = 0 quote = None for ch in body: if quote: cur.append(ch) if ch == quote: quote = None continue if ch in "\"'": quote = ch cur.append(ch) elif ch == "{": depth += 1 cur.append(ch) elif ch == "}": depth = max(0, depth - 1) cur.append(ch) elif ch == sep and depth == 0: parts.append("".join(cur).strip()) cur = [] else: cur.append(ch) if "".join(cur).strip(): parts.append("".join(cur).strip()) return parts def parse_bib(text): """Minimal, tolerant BibTeX parser. Good enough for well-formed entries.""" entries = [] i, n = 0, len(text) while i < n: if text[i] != "@": i += 1 continue j = i + 1 while j < n and (text[j].isalpha() or text[j] == "-"): j += 1 etype = text[i + 1 : j].lower() if etype in ("comment", "preamble", "string"): i = _skip_braced(text, j) continue k = j while k < n and text[k] not in "{[": k += 1 if k >= n: break open_ch = text[k] close_ch = "}" if open_ch == "{" else "]" depth = 0 end = k + 1 for p in range(k + 1, n): c = text[p] if open_ch == "{" and c == "{": depth += 1 elif open_ch == "{" and c == "}": depth -= 1 if depth == 0: end = p break body = text[k + 1 : end] i = end + 1 chunks = _split_top(body) key = chunks[0] if chunks else "" fields = {} for chunk in chunks[1:]: if "=" not in chunk: continue name, value = chunk.split("=", 1) fields[name.strip().lower()] = _clean_value(value) entries.append({"key": key, "type": etype, "fields": fields}) return entries def _skip_braced(text, start): """Advance past a braced group that follows a skipped entry type.""" i = start while i < len(text) and text[i] not in "{[": i += 1 if i >= len(text): return i depth = 0 for p in range(i, len(text)): if text[p] == "{": depth += 1 elif text[p] == "}": depth -= 1 if depth == 0: return p + 1 return len(text) # --------------------------------------------------------------- front matter def split_frontmatter(text): if not text.startswith("---"): return {}, text lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True) end = None for i in range(1, len(lines)): if lines[i].strip() in ("---", "..."): end = i break if end is None: return {}, text yaml_text = "".join(lines[1:end]) body = "".join(lines[end + 1 :]) data = yaml.safe_load(yaml_text) if yaml else None return (data or {}, body) # ------------------------------------------------------------------- authors def split_authors(raw): parts = re.split(r"\s+and\s+", raw) return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()] def flip_name(name): name = name.strip() if "," in name: last, first = name.split(",", 1) return (first.strip() + " " + last.strip()).strip() return name def name_tokens(name): return sorted(set(re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", name.lower()))) # --------------------------------------------------------------------- build def build(): # ---- resume ---- resume_json = json.loads(read(os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "resume.json"))) resume = { "name": resume_json.get("name", ""), "title": resume_json.get("title", ""), "affiliation": resume_json.get("affiliation", ""), "photo": resume_json.get("photo", ""), "email": resume_json.get("email", ""), "about": resume_json.get("about", []), "quick_links": resume_json.get("quick_links", []), "socials": resume_json.get("socials", []), "experience": resume_json.get("experience", []), "education": resume_json.get("education", []), "awards": resume_json.get("awards", []), "thesis": resume_json.get("thesis"), } me_tokens = name_tokens(resume.get("name", "")) # ---- publications ---- raw_entries = parse_bib(read(os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "publications.bib"))) pubs = [] for ent in raw_entries: f = ent["fields"] year = f.get("year", "").strip() try: year_int = int(year) except ValueError: year_int = 0 authors_raw = split_authors(f.get("author", "")) authors = [] for a in authors_raw: display = flip_name(a) authors.append({"name": display, "me": name_tokens(display) == me_tokens and bool(me_tokens)}) venue = f.get("booktitle") or f.get("journal") or f.get("venue") or "" urls = { "paper": f.get("url") or f.get("paper") or f.get("pdf") or f.get("doi"), "project": f.get("project"), "code": f.get("code"), "video": f.get("video"), "slides": f.get("slides"), "supplement": f.get("supplement"), } pubs.append( { "key": ent["key"], "type": ent["type"], "title": norm_ws(f.get("title", ent["key"])), "authors": authors, "venue": norm_ws(venue), "year": year, "_year": year_int, "month": f.get("month", ""), "note": f.get("note", ""), "doi": f.get("doi", ""), "urls": urls, } ) # Group by year, newest first; keep file order within a year. years = sorted({p["_year"] for p in pubs if p["_year"]}, reverse=True) grouped = [] for y in years: grouped.append({"year": str(y), "entries": [p for p in pubs if p["_year"] == y]}) # Any entries without a usable year (shouldn't happen) still get shown. orphans = [p for p in pubs if p["_year"] == 0] if orphans: grouped.append({"year": "Unclassified", "entries": orphans}) # ---- news ---- news = [] for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "news", "*.md"))): text = read(path) fm, body = split_frontmatter(text) date_raw = fm.get("date") or "" iso = str(date_raw).strip() title = fm.get("title") or "" if markdown: html = markdown.markdown(body, extensions=["extra", "sane_lists"]) else: html = "
".join(p for p in [x.strip() for x in body.strip().splitlines()]) news.append( { "date_display": fmt_date(date_raw), "iso": iso, "title": title if title != os.path.basename(path)[:-3] else "", "html": html, } ) news.sort(key=lambda x: x["iso"], reverse=True) # ---- render ---- env = Environment( loader=FileSystemLoader(os.path.join(ROOT, "templates")), autoescape=select_autoescape(["html", "htm"]), trim_blocks=True, lstrip_blocks=True, ) env.globals.get("date") # (no-op; clarity only) tpl = env.get_template("site.html") newest = max( (os.path.getmtime(p) for p in ( glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "data", "*")) + glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "news", "*.md")) + glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "assets", "*")) + glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "templates", "*")) )), default=os.path.getmtime(__file__), ) import time build_date = time.strftime("%d %b %Y", time.localtime(newest)) html = tpl.render( resume=resume, pubs=grouped, pub_count=len(pubs), news=news, build_date=build_date, ) dist = os.path.join(ROOT, "dist") if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(dist, "assets")): shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(dist, "assets")) shutil.copytree(os.path.join(ROOT, "assets"), os.path.join(dist, "assets")) write(os.path.join(dist, "index.html"), html) print(f"OK Wrote {os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dist, 'index.html'), ROOT)}") print(f" publications : {len(pubs)} (across {len(years)} years)") print(f" news items : {len(news)}") print(f" host : any static host (serve the 'dist' directory)") return 0 if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(build())

# Duygu Ceylan - personal website

A small, content-driven static website. Everything on the page is rendered
from a handful of plain-text source files. There is no CMS and no database: to
publish a change you edit a file, run one build command, and copy the output
directory to any static host.

The same conventions used at kaanaksit.com apply here, in a lighter form:

- publications come from a single BibTeX file
- identity, socials, awards, and the thesis come from one JSON file
- news items are one small Markdown file each
- the layout lives in one template

## Layout

    data/           source content (edit these)
      resume.json   who the site is about, socials, awards, education, thesis
      publications.bib   every publication in the "Publications" section
    news/           one Markdown file per announcement
    assets/         the portrait, stylesheet, and a few lines of JavaScript
    templates/      the single-page HTML layout (Jinja2)
    build.py        builds dist/ from the sources above
    dist/           generated output (do not edit; safe to delete)

## Prerequisites

Python 3.9 or newer. The build needs three packages:

    pip install jinja2 markdown pyyaml

(`requirements.txt` lists them for convenience: `pip install -r requirements.txt`.)

## Build

From the project root:

    python3 build.py

This writes the whole site to `dist/`:

    dist/
      index.html
      assets/style.css
      assets/main.js
      assets/profile.jpg

## Preview locally

    python3 build.py
    cd dist && python3 -m http.server 8123

then open http://127.0.0.1:8123/

## How to update each part

### New publication

`data/publications.bib` holds one block per paper. Copy an existing block,
change the first line to a new unique key, and edit the fields. A field you do
not set is simply not shown.

    @inproceedings{yourkey2025,                 % unique key (first token)
      title     = {A Cool New Paper},           % required
      author    = {Some, Alice and Ceylan, Duygu and Other, Bob},
      year      = {2025},                       % required for grouping
      booktitle = {SIGGRAPH 2025},              % venue (conferences and journals)
      note      = {Oral Paper},                 % optional highlight
      url       = {https://arxiv.org/abs/XXXX.XXXXX},   % shown as "Paper"
      project   = {https://example.com},        % optional, shown as "Project"
      code      = {https://github.com/...},     % optional, shown as "Code"
      video     = {https://youtube.com/...},    % optional, shown as "Video"
      slides    = {https://...pdf},             % optional
      supplement = {https://...pdf},            % optional
    }

Notes:

- List authors as `Last, First and Last, First, ...`. The name that matches
  "Duygu Ceylan" (set in resume.json) is automatically highlighted.
- Put the most recent papers at the top of the file. Within a year the file
  order is preserved; the years are grouped newest-first automatically.
- `booktitle` is used for both conferences and journals (for example
  "ACM Transactions on Graphics"). If the venue text already contains the
  year, the year is not repeated; if it does not, it is appended.

### Identity, socials, awards, thesis

`data/resume.json`. All strings may contain simple inline HTML, so you can put
links where you like.

- `about`: an array of paragraphs shown in the header.
- `socials`: an array of `{ "label": ..., "url": ... }`.
- `quick_links`: buttons under the bio (for example the Full CV PDF).
- `experience` and `education`: arrays shown under "Background".
- `awards`: array of `{ "year": ..., "title": ... }`.
- `thesis`: one object for the PhD thesis, including its download `url`.
- `photo`: the file name (inside `assets/`) of the portrait. Replace
  `assets/profile.jpg` with a new image of the same name to swap the photo.

### A news item

Create a new file in `news/`. Suggested name: `YYYY-MM-DD-short-slug.md`.

    ---
    date: 2026-10-13
    title: Short headline (optional)
    ---

    Write the announcement here. Markdown is supported, including links and
    lists.

Items are listed newest first. The `date` front matters is required; `title`
is optional.

## Deployment

`dist/` is a self-contained static directory. Any of the following work:

- Point the `dist/` folder at any web server.
- GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, or S3 by uploading `dist/` on every
  push.
- A `CNAME` file is included so that when this repository is hosted on a
  matching domain the site resolves there.

## Commit messages

Follow the convention `<emoji> <topic>: <message>`, for example:

    ✍️ content: add Track4Gen to SIGGRAPH 2025
    📰 news: announce Eurographics award

messages.summary:
## Objective
Build a programmatic, easy-to-update personal website for the user's wife, Duygu Ceylan, in `/mnt/yedek/bulut/sandbox/duygu_ceylan_website`, so her public info can be updated by editing data files (bib, JSON, markdown) rather than a CMS.

## Requirements
- Initialize a git repository in the current folder; leave the remote blank for now (done; not yet configured).
- Mirror the user's approach from kaanaksit.com: publications from a `*.bib`, resume as JSON, news/links from markdown + YAML.
- User's chosen base (via question tool): "Minimal custom site" (no Jekyll), same data conventions.
- Chosen sections: Publications, Bio/about, Awards, Thesis, News, Contact + socials.
- Seed content: extract her current publications from https://duygu-ceylan.com (done, 58 papers).
- No publication hallucination; verified profile links only.

## Decisions
- Single self-contained Python build (`build.py`, uses jinja2, markdown, pyyaml — all available; no bibtexparser, so a tolerant in-house BibTeX parser was written).
- Single-page layout, one Jinja2 template, CSS in `assets/style.css`, tiny vanilla JS filter in `assets/main.js`.
- Publications grouped by year, newest first; "me" author (Duygu Ceylan) auto-highlighted by name tokens; venue year dedup via `venue_has_year`; client-side search filters entries + year headers.
- Verified external links used in resume.json: Scholar `https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=56Kj2QoAAAAJ`, ORCID `https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2307-9052`, Adobe Research `https://research.adobe.com/person/duygu-ceylan/`, ResearchGate `https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Duygu-Ceylan`, GitHub `https://github.com/duyguceylan`. LinkedIn/DBLP deliberately omitted (IDs unverified).
- Portrait downloaded from her live site (`.../wp-content/uploads/2016/07/profile2.jpg`) to `assets/profile.jpg` (1200x1600 JPEG, ~505 KB).
- Included `CNAME` (`duygu-ceylan.com`) and a minimal GitHub Actions build workflow (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) for later; no remote added.
- `/mnt/yedek/bulut/depolar/ceylan` turned out to be the user's opencode config repo, NOT a website — ignored.

## Work State
### Completed
- Git repo initialized (default branch committed once), no remote configured.
- Site fully built and committed: header/bio, 58 publications (all from the live site), news item, Background, Awards (Eurographics PhD 2015, Young Researcher 2020), EPFL thesis card, Contact.
- Build verified in Firefox (screenshots, snapshot, DOM checks); filter, counts, and year-header hiding tested working.
- Bugs found and fixed: bib brace scanner cut entries at first value (`_read_braced` fix); comment-line `@type` leak (added `strip_comments`); duplicated year in meta line; missing comma before last author (`loop.last` → `loop.first`).
- README.md, requirements.txt, .gitignore written; scratch screenshots and preview server cleaned up; `dist/` regenerated and gitignored.
- Showed the user the rendered page (full page + hero) as requested.

### Active
- Awaiting user's go-ahead for remote hosting choice (target host/account and domain) or further visual/content tweaks.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Ask/wait for the user's hosting target (e.g., GitHub repo URL, Netlify/Cloudflare Pages) and confirm domain (CNAME currently `duygu-ceylan.com`), then configure the git remote and hosting pipeline.
2. If requested, adjust look/content: colors/typography in `assets/style.css`, sections in `data/resume.json`, entries in `data/publications.bib` or `news/` files, then `python3 build.py`.

## Relevant Files
- `/mnt/yedek/bulut/sandbox/duygu_ceylan_website/`: the project (repo root).
- `build.py`: single build script (bib parser, frontmatter, render, copy assets to `dist/`).
- `data/publications.bib`: 58 seeded entries; field conventions documented in its header comment.
- `data/resume.json`: identity, bio paragraphs, socials, quick_links, experience, education, awards, thesis.
- `templates/site.html`: Jinja2 single-page layout (nav, hero, news, publications, background, awards, thesis, contact).
- `assets/style.css`, `assets/main.js`, `assets/profile.jpg`: styling, filter JS, portrait.
- `news/2026-10-13-website-relaunch.md`: news item format example (YAML frontmatter `date` required, `title` optional).
- `README.md`: update/deploy guide.
- `/mnt/yedek/bulut/depolar/kaanaksit.github.io`: user's reference site (jekyll-scholar `_bibliography/papers.bib`, `assets/json/resume.json`, `_news/*.md`) for convention comparison.
- Live source of her content: `https://duygu-ceylan.com` (WordPress; also hosts the Full CV and thesis PDFs already linked in the site).

## Important Context
- Build command: `python3 build.py` from repo root; local preview: `cd dist && python3 -m http.server <port>`.
- Python on path is the `odak` venv python (has jinja2 3.1.6, markdown 3.10.2, PyYAML 6.0.3; no bibtexparser/bs4 — do not add those without checking).
- Firefox devtools `saveTo` only accepts CWD-relative paths or `/home/kaan/.firefox-devtools-mcp/output`; `evaluate_script` takes a `function` key (JS function string); page CSS uses `scroll-behavior: smooth`, so scroll-then-screenshot needs care.
- Git identity on this machine: Kaan Akşit / kunguz@gmail.com; single commit so far: `c160b28` "🛰️ site: scaffold programmatic personal website for Duygu Ceylan"; working tree clean; no remote.
- Old-site asset links (CV PDF, thesis, some 2012–2016 papers) point to `www.duygu-ceylan.com` sub-paths; those URLs will break if the old WordPress site is removed — worth flagging to the user before decommissioning it.
- Her Scholar page lists affiliation as "ADOBE RESEARCH"; her site header says "Principal Research Scientist, Adobe Research London" (kept as-is in resume.json).

Do not use <https://opencode.ai/docs/>, which documents V1, and do not use
general web search to resolve a V2 documentation question when the V2 docs or
linked pages cover it. The schema served from
<https://opencode.ai/config.json> may describe V1 even though V2 configuration
files include that URL for editor integration. Never use it to infer V2 field
names or shapes. If V2 documentation is missing or contradictory, state the
uncertainty or ask for clarification instead of falling back to V1.

V1 documentation and syntax may be consulted only when the user explicitly
asks about V1 or when needed as migration input. Outputs and recommendations
must still use V2 unless the user specifically requests a V1 result.

## [CLI](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli)

For questions about the terminal interface, command-line invocation, `run`,
`mini`, terminal providers, or other CLI behavior, fetch the
[CLI guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli) and the relevant page linked from
that section.

CLI and TUI preferences are separate from OpenCode's server and project
configuration. They live in the global `~/.config/opencode/cli.json`, or
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/opencode/cli.json` when `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is set. There is no
project-local CLI configuration. Set `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` to merge
inline JSON over the global settings. Most preferences can also be changed from
the TUI by pressing `Ctrl+P` and selecting **Open settings**.

### [Settings](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)

Fetch the full [CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config)
before editing `cli.json`. It documents every terminal-only setting, accepted
values, and examples, including themes, input, sessions, tabs, diffs, alerts,
Mini, keybindings, terminal plugins, and debugging. Do not put these settings
in `opencode.json(c)`.

### [Keybinds](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds)

Configure keybindings under `keybinds` in `cli.json`. The leader key is the
`keybinds.leader` entry; leader timing is configured separately under
`leader.timeout`. Bindings can use a string, an array of strings, or an object
when event behavior such as `preventDefault` is required. Disable a binding
with `"none"` or `false`.

Never guess a command ID, default binding, or accepted key syntax. Fetch the
full [keybind reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/keybinds), which lists
the current IDs and defaults, before answering or editing a binding.

## [OpenCode configuration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config)

OpenCode's server and project configuration uses JSON or JSONC. Include the
published schema so the user's editor can validate fields and provide
autocomplete:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
}
```

Global configuration lives at `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)` and applies
to every project for that user. Project configuration can live in any directory
as `opencode.json(c)` or `.opencode/opencode.json(c)`, including nested packages
in a monorepo.

During ordinary project discovery, OpenCode searches the current Location
directory and every ancestor through the filesystem root, including directories
above the detected project or repository root. It merges direct
`opencode.json(c)` files from the farthest ancestor to the current directory,
then does the same for `.opencode/opencode.json(c)` files. This means every
discovered `.opencode` config overrides every discovered direct config. Global
filesystem configuration has lower precedence than these discovered documents.

Common configuration fields include `model`, `default_agent`, `permissions`,
`agents`, `commands`, `plugins`, `providers`, `mcp`, `skills`, `instructions`,
`references`, `formatter`, and `lsp`.

This configuration is distinct from `cli.json`. Use the
[CLI settings reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/cli/config) for terminal
preferences, especially themes and keybindings.

Do not guess field names or shapes. Fetch the V2 configuration guide and its
linked topic guide as the source of truth, and preserve unrelated settings when
editing an existing file. Keep the published `$schema` URL in configuration
examples, but do not fetch it to determine the V2 configuration shape.

See the [full configuration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/config) for
every field, examples, config locations, and links to dedicated feature guides.

## [MCP servers](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/mcp-servers)

Configure MCP servers under `mcp.servers`. Prefer the CLI because it preserves
unrelated configuration. Use `--global` when the user asks to set up a service
for themselves without limiting it to the current project; omit it when they
explicitly want project-local configuration.

```sh
opencode mcp add <name> --global --url <remote-url>
opencode mcp list
```

Remote servers use OAuth by default. If `mcp list` reports that a server needs
authentication, tell the user to run `/mcps`, select the server, and sign in.
Do not run `opencode mcp auth` through the shell tool: it starts an interactive
flow whose authorization link can be hidden in background process output.
Use the user-facing MCP interface instead.

Report the server as configured but awaiting sign-in until its connection
status confirms it is connected.

OAuth credentials are stored outside the OpenCode configuration. Do not ask for or
store an API key when the server supports OAuth. Use header-based credentials
only when OAuth is unavailable or the user explicitly requires them, and use an
environment substitution such as `{env:MCP_API_KEY}` instead of writing a
secret into configuration.

## [V1 to V2 migration](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1)

For any request to migrate OpenCode configuration, agents, commands, skills,
plugins, integrations, or other behavior from V1 to V2, read the full
[migration guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/migrate-v1) before acting. In
the repository, its source is `services/www/src/docs/content/migrate-v1.mdx`.

V1 config files and `.opencode/` definitions are intended to remain compatible.
The only intentional breaking changes are the server API and plugin API. Native
V2 config uses more ergonomic shapes, but conversion is optional. When the user
requests conversion, inspect the complete configuration, preserve behavior and
unrelated settings, and apply only the relevant migrations from the guide. For
plugin migrations, fetch and follow both the migration guide and the full
[plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins). If non-API V1
functionality fails in V2, use the `report` skill to file it as a compatibility
bug.

## [Plugins](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)

For questions about creating, configuring, loading, publishing, or migrating
plugins, fetch the full [plugins guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins)
before answering. Refer to this guide when the user wants to build a plugin. It
covers hooks, transforms, tools, plugin context capabilities, and package
entrypoints. Plugins can also extend the TUI; for those, fetch the
[CLI plugin guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/cli).
For custom methods and events shared with other plugins or clients, fetch the
[RPC guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/plugins/rpc).

## [Service](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting#check-the-background-service)

OpenCode uses a client-server architecture. Interfaces such as the TUI connect
to a background OpenCode service, which owns sessions, configuration, plugins,
permissions, and tool execution.

OpenCode normally discovers or starts the shared background service
automatically. If the service is stuck or unhealthy, restart it:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

Check its status after restarting:

```sh
opencode service status
```

## [API](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api)

OpenCode exposes an HTTP API from its server. The API is described by an
OpenAPI document available from the running server at `/openapi.json`.

Use OpenCode's built-in `api` command for local requests. It uses the same
discovery and authentication flow as the TUI and may start the background
service when no compatible healthy service is available. It accepts either an
HTTP method and path or an OpenAPI operation ID.

Call an endpoint with an HTTP method and path:

```sh
opencode api get /api/info
```

Pass a request body with `--data` or `-d`, and additional headers with
`--header` or `-H`:

```sh
opencode api post /api/example --data '{"key":"value"}'
opencode api get /api/example --header 'X-Example:value'
```

Request bodies default to `Content-Type: application/json`. When OpenCode is
connected to an explicit server instead of its managed background service, use
the same configured server and authentication context rather than constructing
an unauthenticated request separately.

See the [full API reference](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/api) for available
endpoints, parameters, request bodies, and response schemas. The
raw [OpenAPI specification](https://opencode.ai/v2/openapi.json) is also
available for code generation and other tooling.

## [Client](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client)

For questions about connecting an application to OpenCode over the network,
fetch the full [client guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/client) before
answering.

`@opencode/client` is the generated TypeScript client for the OpenCode HTTP
API. Its methods and types come from the same contract as the API reference.
The default entrypoint exposes Promise-based resource clients and async
iterables for streaming endpoints. The `@opencode/client/effect` entrypoint
exposes typed Effects, Streams, and decoded OpenCode schema values. Its
`Service` API can discover, start, stop, and authenticate with the local
background service from a Node application.

## [SDK](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk)

For questions about embedding OpenCode directly in an application, fetch the
full [SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk) before answering. The SDK
hosts OpenCode in the application without opening an HTTP listener.

Use the [Effect SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/effect) for
Effect applications. For Cloudflare Durable Objects, use the
[Cloudflare SDK guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/build/sdk/cloudflare).

## [Troubleshooting](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)

OpenCode runs a client and a background server. Start by determining whether a
problem belongs to the client, the shared server, or one project.

- Check the service with `opencode service status` and verify the API with
  `opencode api get /api/info`.
- Compare with `opencode --standalone`, which runs the TUI with a private
  server, to isolate shared-service issues.
- Inspect `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`. Filter `role=cli` for
  client startup and `role=server` for sessions, providers, plugins,
  permissions, and tools.
- Run one reproduction with `OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG` when normal logs are not
  sufficient.
- Do not delete or edit the database, service registration, or service config
  while diagnosing a problem. Back up persistent data before inspecting it
  with external tools.
- Redact API keys, authorization headers, prompts, file contents, and other
  sensitive data before sharing diagnostics.

See the [full troubleshooting guide](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/troubleshooting)
for service lifecycle commands, API inspection, log locations, explicit server
connections, issue-reporting details, and local development paths.

Starts the minimal interactive interface instead of the full-screen TUI.

```bash
$ opencode mini
```

Continue the last session.

```bash
$ opencode mini --continue
```

Start with a model and an initial prompt.

```bash
$ opencode mini --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 --prompt "Summarize this repository"
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode mini --help
```

## session

Manages sessions.

```bash
$ opencode session list
```

Limit the list and print JSON.

```bash
$ opencode session list --max-count 20 --format json
```

Delete a session and its child sessions.

```bash
$ opencode session delete ses_9c1b08
```

Export session data as JSON.

```bash
$ opencode session export ses_4f2a1c
```

Redact sensitive transcript and file data when exporting.

```bash
$ opencode session export ses_4f2a1c --sanitize
```

Import session data from a JSON file or URL.

```bash
$ opencode session import session.json
```

Import into a specific directory.

```bash
$ opencode session import session.json --directory ~/code/project
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode session --help
```

## auth

Manages AI providers and credentials.

```bash
$ opencode auth list
```

List them as JSON.

```bash
$ opencode auth list --format json
```

Log in to a provider.

```bash
$ opencode auth login anthropic
```

Log in with a specific authentication method.

```bash
$ opencode auth login anthropic --method key
```

Log out of a saved account.

```bash
$ opencode auth logout anthropic work
```

Switch the active account for an integration.

```bash
$ opencode auth switch anthropic work
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode auth --help
```

## models

Lists every available model.

```bash
$ opencode models
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode models --help
```

## mcp

Manages MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers.

```bash
$ opencode mcp list
```

Add a remote server.

```bash
$ opencode mcp add context7 --url https://mcp.context7.com/mcp
```

Add a local server to the global config.

```bash
$ opencode mcp add everything --global -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything
```

Add a local server with an environment variable.

```bash
$ opencode mcp add everything --env LOG_LEVEL=debug -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything
```

Add a remote server with a header.

```bash
$ opencode mcp add context7 --url https://mcp.context7.com/mcp --header CONTEXT7_API_KEY=secret
```

Authenticate with an OAuth-capable remote server.

```bash
$ opencode mcp auth sentry
```

Remove stored OAuth credentials for a server.

```bash
$ opencode mcp logout sentry
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode mcp --help
```

## plugin

Manages plugins.

```bash
$ opencode plugin list
```

Include built-in server plugins.

```bash
$ opencode plugin list --builtin
```

Install a plugin and add it to the global configuration.

```bash
$ opencode plugin add @example/opencode-tui
```

Check package plugins for updates.

```bash
$ opencode plugin check
```

Update package plugins.

```bash
$ opencode plugin update
```

Remove a plugin from global configuration.

```bash
$ opencode plugin remove @example/opencode-tui
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode plugin --help
```

## stats

Shows shareable usage statistics.

```bash
$ opencode stats
```

Show the last 7 days.

```bash
$ opencode stats --days 7
```

Show model usage.

```bash
$ opencode stats --models
```

Show cost and token details.

```bash
$ opencode stats --cost
```

Print JSON instead of a report.

```bash
$ opencode stats --json
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode stats --help
```

## serve

Starts the API and web server. See [Web](/cli/web).

```bash
$ opencode serve
```

Bind to all interfaces on a fixed port.

```bash
$ opencode serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096
```

Allow a browser client from another origin.

```bash
$ opencode serve --cors https://app.example.com
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode serve --help
```

## pair

Prints one-time links, plus a QR code of the first one, that sign a browser or
app in to the server. Links expire after 5 minutes and work once.

```bash
$ opencode pair
```

Use an external URL in the links.

```bash
$ opencode pair --url https://dev.example.com
```

Pair from anywhere through an OpenTunnel remote address. This exposes the
server to the internet, so the first time it enables remote access it explains
this and asks you to accept. See [Remote access](/cli/web#remote-access).

```bash
$ opencode pair --remote
```

Accept without a prompt, for example in a script without a terminal.

```bash
$ opencode pair --remote --yes
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode pair --help
```

## service

Manages the background server. See [Web](/cli/web).

```bash
$ opencode service start
```

Restart it.

```bash
$ opencode service restart
```

Show its status.

```bash
$ opencode service status
```

Stop it.

```bash
$ opencode service stop
```

Read a setting.

```bash
$ opencode service get hostname
```

Set a setting.

```bash
$ opencode service set hostname 0.0.0.0
```

Allow an extra CORS origin.

```bash
$ opencode service set cors https://app.example.com
```

Pass an environment variable to the server process.

```bash
$ opencode service set env OPENCODE_LOG_LEVEL DEBUG
```

Reset a setting to its default.

```bash
$ opencode service unset hostname
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode service --help
```

## reload

Reloads configuration without restarting the server. Running sessions continue with fresh services at the next step boundary.

```bash
$ opencode reload
```

## api

Makes a request to the running server.

```bash
$ opencode api GET /api/session
```

Call an operation ID with a query parameter.

```bash
$ opencode api session.list --param limit=10
```

Send a JSON body.

```bash
$ opencode api session.create --data '{"title": "New session"}'
```

Add a request header.

```bash
$ opencode api GET /api/session -H "accept: application/json"
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode api --help
```

## acp

Starts an Agent Client Protocol server over stdin and stdout for editor integrations. It runs until the client closes the connection.

```bash
$ opencode acp
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode acp --help
```

## debug

Provides debugging and troubleshooting tools.

```bash
$ opencode debug agents
```

List configuration sources.

```bash
$ opencode debug config
```

Show global paths.

```bash
$ opencode debug paths
```

Print a single path.

```bash
$ opencode debug paths db
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode debug --help
```

## upgrade

Upgrades OpenCode to the latest or a specific version. Alias: `update`.

```bash
$ opencode upgrade
```

Upgrade to a specific version with a specific package manager.

```bash
$ opencode upgrade 2.0.21 --method bun
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode upgrade --help
```

## uninstall

Removes OpenCode and all related files.

```bash
$ opencode uninstall
```

Preview what would be removed.

```bash
$ opencode uninstall --dry-run
```

View all subcommands and flags.

```bash
$ opencode uninstall --help
```

DESCRIPTION
  Export session data as JSON

USAGE
  opencode session export [flags] [<session>]

ARGUMENTS
  session string    Session ID to export (optional)

FLAGS
  --standalone       Run with a private server instead of the background service
  --server string    Connect to a server URL instead of the background service
  --sanitize         Redact sensitive transcript and file data

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h                                                          Show help information
  --version, -v                                                       Show version information
  --wizard                                                            Start wizard mode for a command
  --completions <bash|zsh|fish|sh>                                    Print shell completion script (choices: bash, zsh, fish, sh)
  --log-level <all|trace|debug|info|warn|warning|error|fatal|none>    Sets the minimum log level (choices: all, trace, debug, info, warn, warning, error, fatal, none)
  --print-logs                                                        Print logs to stderr (server logs require --standalone)
---- import help (for the other machine) ----
DESCRIPTION
  Import session data from a JSON file or URL

USAGE
  opencode session import [flags] <file>

ARGUMENTS
  file string    JSON file or URL to import

FLAGS
  --standalone          Run with a private server instead of the background service
  --server string       Connect to a server URL instead of the background service
  --directory string    Directory in which to import the session

GLOBAL FLAGS
  --help, -h                                                          Show help information
  --version, -v                                                       Show version information
  --wizard                                                            Start wizard mode for a command
  --completions <bash|zsh|fish|sh>                                    Print shell completion script (choices: bash, zsh, fish, sh)
  --log-level <all|trace|debug|info|warn|warning|error|fatal|none>    Sets the minimum log level (choices: all, trace, debug, info, warn, warning, error, fatal, none)
  --print-logs                                                        Print logs to stderr (server logs require --standalone)
